mainTopic: The end of the proof about שני עושה שלישי בחולין, the argument over תחומי שבת, and how בני ישראל sang שירת הים.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a proof about what רבי אליעזר holds on whether a שני can make a שלישי in חולין. The proof uses his argument with the חכמים about linking pure and impure dough to separate חלה, together with a ברייתא that allows a middle piece as big as a כביצה. רב מרי rejects the proof: the argument might instead be about whether dough still owing חלה is treated like חלה. A second answer says the argument might be about whether one may cause impurity to חולין in ארץ ישראל. The גמרא then turns to another teaching from 'that day' in the משנה and explains that רבי עקיבא and רבי אליעזר בנו של רבי יוסי הגלילי disagree about whether תחומי שבת are דאורייתא or דרבנן. Next comes a three-way argument about how בני ישראל sang שירת הים: with a refrain, by repeating every word, or with משה starting and everyone singing together. Each view comes from a different reading of ״וַיֹּאמְרוּ לֵאמֹר״. The amud ends with teachings that even nursing babies sang at the sea, and that even unborn babies did. רבי מאיר begins bringing a פסוק for that last point, and the פסוק continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The Sages forbid the method
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה ends: the חכמים forbid the method רבי אליעזר allowed for separating חלה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the משנה the גמרא is quoting. רבי אליעזר allowed placing pure dough in the middle to link the doughs for separating חלה, and the חכמים forbid it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are now two sides to compare: רבי אליעזר permits and the חכמים forbid. The rest of the סוגיא will try to work out what reasoning lies behind this disagreement.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of dough that must be given to a כהן

phrases.english: And the Sages forbid it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quotation of the משנה that the proof is built on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים forbid using pure dough in the middle to link the doughs for separating חלה.

steps.title: A ברייתא allows even an egg-bulk
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that according to רבי אליעזר, the pure dough placed in the middle may be as large as a כביצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught in a ברייתא: an egg-bulk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a ברייתא that changes the size in the case. The middle piece of pure dough can be a full כביצה, not only less than that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food smaller than a כביצה cannot pass impurity on to other food, so a small middle piece would raise no question. A full כביצה can become impure and also pass impurity on. That makes the case useful as a proof, because now we must explain why the impurity does not spread onward to the pure dough.

keyTerms.meaning: The size of an egg, the smallest amount of food that can become impure

steps.confusionAlert: The size matters here. Less than a כביצה cannot pass impurity on to other food, but a full כביצה can. That is why the ברייתא turns this case into a real proof.

phrases.english: And it was taught: an egg-bulk.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא means the middle piece of pure dough may be a full egg-bulk, which is big enough to become impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא that enlarges the middle piece so that it can become impure.
steps.raayaObject: What רבי אליעזר holds about שני עושה שלישי בחולין
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating that the middle piece may be a כביצה

steps.title: The assumptions behind the proof
steps.stepSummary: The people bringing the proof assumed that the impure dough is a ראשון, and that dough still owing חלה is treated as ordinary חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: They assumed that both this source and that one are talking about dough that is impure in the first degree. They also assumed that חולין still owing חלה is not treated like חלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the proof by listing its starting assumptions. It is preparing the next step, where the proof itself is made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two assumptions. First, the impure dough is a ראשון, so whatever touches it becomes a שני. Second, dough that still owes חלה is ordinary חולין, not holy food like חלה, so the question of a שלישי in חולין applies to it.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this one and that one
Still owing חלה, since it has not yet been separated
Are similar to, are treated like

steps.confusionAlert: The word סברוה is a hint that these are only assumptions, so do not treat them as settled facts. In step 6, רב מרי challenges the second one, that dough still owing חלה is treated as plain חולין.

phrases.english: They assumed that both this one and that one
phrases.notes: 'This one and that one' means the משנה and the ברייתא.

phrases.english: are about dough of first-degree impurity,
and that ordinary food still owing חלה
is not treated like חלה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the assumptions needed to turn the משנה and ברייתא into a proof.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Assumptions: the impure dough is a ראשון, and dough still owing חלה has the status of חולין.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר holds a שני cannot make a שלישי in חולין
steps.stepSummary: The proof begins: the dispute must be whether a שני can make a שלישי in חולין, and רבי אליעזר holds it cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not that they disagree about this: one Sage holds that a second-degree item does not make a third degree in ordinary food,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now makes the proof. It suggests that רבי אליעזר allows the method because he holds that a שני cannot create a שלישי in חולין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pure כביצה in the middle touches the impure dough, which is a ראשון, so the middle piece becomes a שני. If a שני cannot make a שלישי in חולין, the pure dough on the other side stays pure, so the method is fine. The view of the חכמים comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not that, which opens a suggested proof
Ordinary food that is not holy

steps.whyThisMatters: If this proof works, we learn that רבי אליעזר holds impurity in חולין stops at the second degree. That is the question this whole סוגיא is asking.

phrases.english: Is it not that they disagree about this:
that one Sage holds:
phrases.notes: 'One Sage' here is רבי אליעזר, who allowed the method.

phrases.english: a second-degree item does not make a third degree in ordinary food,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the assumptions from step 3 to explain why רבי אליעזר permits the method.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אליעזר's view on whether a שני can make a שלישי in חולין
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה together with the ברייתא allowing a כביצה in the middle

steps.title: The חכמים hold that a שני can make a שלישי in חולין
steps.stepSummary: The proof finishes. The חכמים hold that a שני does make a שלישי in חולין, so they forbid the method.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other Sage (the חכמים) holds that a שני makes a שלישי in חולין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof it started in the last step. It says the חכמים take the opposite side: a שני can pass impurity on and make a שלישי in חולין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The middle piece touches the impure dough, which is a ראשון, so the middle piece becomes a שני. The חכמים say this שני can then make the pure dough a שלישי, so they forbid the method. רבי אליעזר says it cannot, so he allows it.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary food that is not holy (not תרומה or קדשים)
"One Sage holds". Used to set out each side of an argument

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the conclusion that the next steps will push back on. Once the proof is finished, the גמרא can show that the argument could be about something else.

phrases.english: And the other Sage holds:
phrases.notes: This "other Sage" is the חכמים, who forbid רבי אליעזר's method.

phrases.english: a second-degree item makes a third-degree item in ordinary food.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָר סָבַר: שֵׁנִי עוֹשֶׂה שְׁלִישִׁי בְּחוּלִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided proof begun in step 4 by giving the חכמים' position.
steps.raayaObject: The argument between רבי אליעזר and the חכמים is about whether a שני makes a שלישי in חולין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא allowing a middle piece as large as a כביצה, read together with the assumptions from step 3.

steps.title: רב מרי: the argument is about dough that still owes חלה
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי בריה דרב כהנא says everyone agrees that a שני does not make a שלישי in חולין. The argument is about whether חולין הטבולין לחלה are treated like חלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי בריה דרב כהנא said: Everyone agrees that a שני does not make a שלישי in חולין. Here they argue about חולין that still owe חלה. One Sage (the חכמים) holds that this food is like חלה. The other Sage (רבי אליעזר) holds that it is not like חלה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי rejects the proof. He says the argument is not about the rule for חולין at all. It is about the special status of dough from which חלה has not yet been taken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 assumed that dough still owing חלה counts as plain חולין. רב מרי challenges exactly that assumption. If the חכמים treat such dough like חלה, which is holy, then a שני can make it a שלישי. That explains why they forbid the method, even though everyone agrees about plain חולין.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary dough from which חלה has not yet been separated
They are similar to, treated like

steps.confusionAlert: רב מרי is not saying the חכמים think a שני makes a שלישי in plain חולין. He agrees with everyone that it does not. He only says this particular dough might be treated like חלה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב מָרִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Mari, son of Rav Kahana, said:
Everyone agrees
a second-degree item does not make a third-degree item in ordinary food,
and here they argue about ordinary food that still owes חלה.
One Sage holds: it is like חלה,
phrases.notes: This is the חכמים, so for them the pure dough can become a שלישי.

phrases.english: and the other Sage holds: it is not like חלה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מָרִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of steps 4-5 by moving the argument to a different issue.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the conclusion that the argument proves anything about whether a שני makes a שלישי in plain חולין.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed that dough still owing חלה counts as plain חולין. The חכמים may treat it like חלה.

steps.title: Another answer: the argument is about causing impurity to ordinary food in Israel
steps.stepSummary: A second rejection: everyone agrees on both earlier points. The argument is whether you may cause impurity to חולין in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say this instead: Everyone agrees that חולין that still owe חלה are not like חלה. Everyone also agrees that a שני does not make a שלישי in חולין. Here they argue about whether it is allowed to cause impurity to חולין in ארץ ישראל. One Sage (רבי אליעזר) holds that it is allowed. The other Sage (the חכמים) holds that it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different way to reject the proof. Now the argument is not about impurity rules at all. It is about whether you may make ordinary food in ארץ ישראל impure on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here everyone agrees that the pure dough will stay pure. The question is about the middle piece, which itself becomes impure by touching the impure dough. רבי אליעזר allows causing that impurity, but the חכמים forbid it, and that is why they reject the method.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say this instead. It introduces a second possible answer

steps.whatToRemember: The argument in the משנה can be explained three ways: (1) whether a שני makes a שלישי in חולין; (2) whether dough that still owes חלה is like חלה (רב מרי); (3) whether you may cause impurity to חולין in ארץ ישראל.
steps.whyThisMatters: Since the argument can be explained in other ways, the משנה cannot serve as a proof that a שני makes a שלישי in חולין.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
everyone agrees that ordinary food that still owes חלה
is not like חלה,
and a second-degree item does not make a third-degree item in ordinary food,
and here they argue about whether it is allowed to cause impurity
to ordinary food that is in the Land of Israel.
One Sage holds: it is allowed to cause impurity
phrases.notes: This is רבי אליעזר. The middle piece becomes impure, but he doesn't mind.

phrases.english: to ordinary food in the Land of Israel,
and the other Sage holds: it is forbidden to cause impurity
phrases.notes: This is the חכמים. For them, making the middle piece impure is the problem.

phrases.english: to ordinary food in the Land of Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא חוּלִּין הַטְּבוּלִין לְחַלָּה לָא כְּחַלָּה דָּמוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, independent rejection of the proof, accepting both points that the earlier explanations relied on.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof completely: neither impurity question needs to be in dispute.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof ignored a separate reason to forbid the method: the ban on causing impurity to חולין in ארץ ישראל, since the middle piece itself becomes impure.

steps.title: What is the real argument behind the two readings?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about רבי עקיבא's teaching on the Levite cities and asks what practical point the two תנאים disagree about.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'On that day רבי עקיבא taught, etc.' What exactly do they disagree about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. It then asks a question to set up the next step: what is the real point of disagreement?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי עקיבא read the פסוקים about the land around the Levite cities as a source for the שבת limit. רבי אליעזר בנו של רבי יוסי הגלילי read the same פסוקים as being about different kinds of land. The גמרא wants to know what halachic difference stands behind these two readings.

keyTerms.meaning: On that same day (the day רבן גמליאל was removed and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה became head)

phrases.aramaic: בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: On that day Rabbi Akiva expounded, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה about the land around the Levite cities, which רבי עקיבא used for the 2,000 אמה שבת limit.

phrases.english: In what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the earlier discussion about טומאה and חולין and opens a new line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What halachic difference lies behind the two different readings of the פסוקים about the Levite cities?

steps.title: Are תחומי שבת דאורייתא or דרבנן?
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא holds תחומין are from the Torah; רבי אליעזר בנו של רבי יוסי הגלילי holds they are rabbinic.
steps.simpleTranslation: One Sage holds that the שבת boundaries (תחומין) are from the Torah, and the other Sage holds they are from the Rabbis.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The two תנאים argue about whether the Shabbat limit is a Torah law or a rabbinic law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא learns the 2,000 אמה limit from a פסוק, so for him it is דאורייתא. רבי אליעזר בנו של רבי יוסי הגלילי uses the פסוק for something else, which shows that for him the limit is only דרבנן. So the different readings come from a real halachic argument.

keyTerms.meaning: שבת boundaries: the distance you may walk outside your town on שבת

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא: תחומין are דאורייתא. רבי אליעזר בנו של רבי יוסי הגלילי: תחומין are דרבנן.

phrases.english: One Sage holds: Shabbat boundaries are from the Torah,
phrases.notes: The first מר is רבי עקיבא; the second is רבי אליעזר בנו של רבי יוסי הגלילי.

phrases.english: and the other Sage holds: they are from the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They argue whether תחומין are דאורייתא (רבי עקיבא) or דרבנן (רבי אליעזר בנו של רבי יוסי הגלילי).

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the people repeated only the opening line
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings another teaching of רבי עקיבא from that day: at the sea, משה sang and the people kept answering 'אשירה לה׳', like a congregation answering an adult leading הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: On that day רבי עקיבא taught: when Israel came up from the sea, they wanted to sing. How did they sing? Like an adult who leads הלל, and the people answer after him only the opening line. משה said 'I will sing to ה׳' and they said 'I will sing to ה׳‎.' משה said 'For He is highly exalted' and they again said 'I will sing to ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with another teaching of רבי עקיבא from that same day. It explains how בני ישראל sang שירת הים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא compares משה to an adult leading הלל, whose words count for everyone listening. So the people did not need to say every word. They just kept answering the opening line, 'אשירה לה׳', after each phrase משה said.

keyTerms.meaning: Song of praise, here שירת הים
One who leads the reading of הלל for others
Chapter headings, the opening line repeated as a refrain

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
On that day Rabbi Akiva expounded:
At the time that Israel came up from the sea,
they set their eyes on saying a song.
And how did they say the song?
Like an adult who leads the reading of Hallel,
and they answer after him the chapter headings.
phrases.notes: They keep repeating just the opening line, like a refrain.

phrases.english: Moses said: “I will sing to the Lord,”
and they said: “I will sing to the Lord.”
Moses said: “For He is highly exalted,”
and they said: “I will sing to the Lord.”

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another teaching that רבי עקיבא gave on that same day, on a new subject.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At the sea משה led the song like an adult leading הלל, and the people answered only 'אשירה לה׳' after each phrase.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: the people repeated every word
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בנו של רבי יוסי הגלילי says the people sang like those repeating after a child leading הלל, saying every word משה said.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בנו של רבי יוסי הגלילי says: Like a child who leads הלל, and the people repeat after him everything he says. משה said 'I will sing to ה׳' and they said 'I will sing to ה׳‎.' משה said 'For He is highly exalted' and they said 'For He is highly exalted.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא disagrees with רבי עקיבא about how the song was sung. He says the people repeated every phrase after משה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a child leads הלל, his words do not count for the adults listening, so they must repeat every word themselves. רבי אליעזר בנו של רבי יוסי הגלילי says the song at the sea worked this way. So the difference is: did the people answer with a refrain (רבי עקיבא), or did they repeat each phrase (רבי אליעזר)?
steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא: like an adult leading הלל, so the people answered only 'אשירה לה׳'. רבי אליעזר בנו של רבי יוסי הגלילי: like a child leading הלל, so the people repeated every word.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי אליעזר is calling משה a child. The comparison is only about the way the people answered: word for word, as one does after a child.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, says:
Like a minor who leads the reading of Hallel,
phrases.notes: A child's reading does not count for the adults, so they must say every word themselves.

phrases.aramaic: וְהֵן עוֹנִין אַחֲרָיו כׇּל מָה שֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר.
phrases.english: and they repeat after him everything he says.
Moses said: “I will sing to the Lord,”
and they said: “I will sing to the Lord.”
Moses said: “For He is highly exalted,”
and they said: “For He is highly exalted.”

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different opinion on the same question step 10 answered: how the song was sung.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The people repeated every phrase after משה, as one repeats after a child leading הלל.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה: משה Started and Everyone Sang Together
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה says the people sang like a congregation with a שליח ציבור who leads the blessings of שמע. He starts, they repeat the opening, and then everyone continues together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה says: it was like a leader who leads the congregation in שמע in the synagogue. He begins first, and they answer after him.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a third opinion about how the people sang שירת הים, added after רבי עקיבא and רבי אליעזר בנו של רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי עקיבא, the people only repeated a refrain. For רבי אליעזר, they repeated every word after משה. For רבי נחמיה, משה only started the song, and then all of them sang the whole song together with him.

keyTerms.meaning: Leading the congregation in the blessings of שמע
Here: the community leader who leads the prayers
Opens first; starts before everyone else

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 11. There the people repeated each word after משה. Here משה only opens, and after that everyone sings together.

phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya says:
Like a scribe who leads the recital of Shema
in the synagogue,
who begins first
and they answer after him.
phrases.notes: They repeat his opening words, and then everyone keeps going together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third opinion to the argument from steps 10-11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה opened the song, and then all of ישראל sang it together in unison.

steps.title: What Is the Root of Their Argument?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the three תנאים are really arguing about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move: it asks what source or reading lies behind the three opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three describe the same event, so the גמרא wants to know what in the text leads each one to his view. The answer will come from how each reads the words of the פסוק.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the three opinions in steps 10-12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which reading of the פסוק makes each תנא hold his view.

steps.title: Each View Comes from Reading ״וַיֹּאמְרוּ לֵאמֹר״ Differently
steps.stepSummary: The argument depends on how to read ״וַיֹּאמְרוּ לֵאמֹר״ (שמות 15:1). For רבי עקיבא, לאמר points to the first words only. For רבי אליעזר, it points to every word. For רבי נחמיה, ויאמרו means all sang together and לאמר means משה started first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא holds that 'saying' refers to the first words, which the people kept repeating. רבי אליעזר בנו של רבי יוסי הגלילי holds that 'saying' refers to every single word. רבי נחמיה holds that 'and they said' means they all said it together, and 'saying' means משה opened first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by showing how each תנא reads the words of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word לאמר shows that the people's singing was somehow connected to משה's. רבי עקיבא connects it only to the opening line, so the people repeated a refrain. רבי אליעזר connects it to every word, and רבי נחמיה uses ויאמרו for singing together and לאמר only for משה starting first.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Saying': the key word in the פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: One פסוק, three readings. The refrain (רבי עקיבא), every word repeated (רבי אליעזר), or משה starts and all sing together (רבי נחמיה).

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva holds:
'Saying' refers to the first words.
phrases.notes: The word comes from שמות 15:1, ״וַיֹּאמְרוּ לֵאמֹר״. The first words are ״אָשִׁירָה לַה׳״.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי סָבַר:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, holds:
'Saying' refers to each and every word,
and Rabbi Nechemya holds:
'And they said' means that all of them said it together,
'saying' means that Moshe opened first.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each תנא reads ויאמרו and לאמר in שמות 15:1 differently, which produces the three ways of singing.

steps.title: Even Nursing Babies Saw the שכינה and Sang
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי יוסי הגלילי taught that when ישראל came up from the sea they wanted to sing. Even babies on their mothers' laps and nursing infants saw the שכינה, lifted their heads, and said ״זֶה אֵלִי וְאַנְוֵהוּ״, as תהלים says.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: רבי יוסי הגלילי explained that when ישראל came up from the sea, they set their minds on singing. How did they sing? A baby was lying on his mother's knees and an infant was nursing at his mother's breast. When they saw the שכינה, the baby lifted his neck and the infant let go of the breast, and they said ״זֶה אֵלִי וְאַנְוֵהוּ״. As it says, 'From the mouths of babies and nursing infants You have founded strength.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that adds another teaching about שירת הים: even the tiny children took part in the song.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the babies sang because they saw the שכינה, and the words they said were ״זֶה אֵלִי וְאַנְוֵהוּ״. The פסוק in תהלים is brought as support that praise of הקב״ה came from the mouths of babies and nursing infants.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is my God and I will glorify Him'
Set their minds on; decided to

steps.whatToRemember: At the sea, everyone sang, down to the nursing infants, because they all saw the שכינה.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן, דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי:
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili expounded:
At the time that Israel came up from the sea
they set their eyes on saying a song.
And how did they say the song?
A baby lying on his mother's knees,
and an infant nursing from his mother's breasts.
Once they saw the Divine Presence,
the baby lifted his neck,
and the infant let the breast slip from his mouth,
and they said, 'This is my God and I will glorify Him,'
as it is said: 'From the mouths of babies and nursing infants You have founded strength.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן, דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the argument about how the song was sung and brings a new teaching about who sang it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even babies and nursing infants saw the שכינה at the sea and sang ״זֶה אֵלִי וְאַנְוֵהוּ״.

steps.title: Even unborn babies sang at the sea
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר teaches that even עוברים in their mothers' wombs sang the שירה at the sea, and begins to bring a פסוק as proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר used to say: How do we know that even babies still inside their mothers sang the song at the sea? Because the פסוק says:
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר adds a bigger claim than the one before: even unborn babies sang. This line sets up the proof, and the פסוק itself comes right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 15, רבי יוסי הגלילי went as far as babies on laps and nursing infants. רבי מאיר pushes it further, to babies not yet born. The word מנין shows he will prove this from a פסוק, not just state it.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know? (asks for a source in the פסוקים)
That are inside their mother's womb
The song, here meaning the song at the sea

steps.confusionAlert: מנין looks like a question, but רבי מאיר is not unsure. It is his way of saying 'here is my source,' and he answers it himself with a פסוק.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir would say:
From where do we know that even fetuses
in their mother's womb recited the song?
As it is stated:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 15 by widening who sang at the sea, from babies and nursing infants to babies still in the womb.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even עוברים in their mothers' wombs sang the שירה at the sea, and this is learned from a פסוק.
